subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — plugin emission API and manifest policy

question: Should OpenClaw expose an external-plugin AI-safety telemetry capability, and if so must identity, trust, manifest permissions, event validation, and session attribution all remain host-owned?
rationale: This creates a permanent public plugin contract and a privileged path into operator-facing security telemetry; automation cannot choose the trust model or taxonomy ownership safely.

options.title: Sponsor a host-owned capability
options.body: Approve the taxonomy direction but require a runtime-injected closure bound to the loaded plugin and active session, with parsed manifest permissions and full payload validation.

options.title: Keep detectors plugin-local
options.body: Do not add a core telemetry authority yet; external detectors can use existing plugin hooks and their own observability until a narrower core requirement is established.

options.title: Accept caller-supplied authority
options.body: Land the standalone helper and explicitly own the spoofing, attribution, and long-term plugin compatibility risks it introduces.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a host-owned capability
recommendation.body: Approve the taxonomy direction but require a runtime-injected closure bound to the loaded plugin and active session, with parsed manifest permissions and full payload validation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent plugin manifest and install-contract history plus adjacent product/security review context make this the strongest available routing candidate.
